title: Entitlement rollback safety net and SIEM validation checklist
content:
Summary:
This doc specifies a safety-net plan for rolling back entitlement changes during RBAC v2 rollout, plus a compact SIEM validation checklist and sample audit payloads to verify evidence automation ingestion. Goal: allow Product/Platform to revert authorization surface changes safely with clear signals in SIEM and minimal blast radius for customers and infra.

Background & motivation:
- RBAC v2 introduces attribute-driven grants, epoched entitlements, and a staged backfill of legacy coarse grants.
- During earlier experiments we observed two classes of failures: (1) incorrect attribute mapping that silently widens permissions, and (2) backfill jobs that temporarily remove an entitlement due to race conditions. Both need safe, fast rollback paths and high-confidence SIEM signals.
- We need to treat entitlement migration like a DB schema migration: staged, reversible, observable. This doc prescribes a template for rollback triggers, automated mitigation, and SIEM validation queries to detect regressions within 15 minutes of changes.

Key definitions (for this doc):
- entitlement epoch: an immutable snapshot of the computed effective entitlements for a tenant at a given time.
- entitlement backfill job: process that computes new entitlements from attributes and writes to the entitlement store.
- entitlement delta: set of grant/remove operations between two epochs.
- rollback window: time period after a rollout where automated rollback is permitted (default: 2 hours).

Rollback strategy overview:
1) Canary + epoch-based release: apply new entitlement logic to a canary subset producing epoch N+1 while serving epoch N for traffic. Only switch serving epoch after smoke checks pass.
2) Graceful dual-read mode: for 30 minutes after switch, runtime consults both epochs for deny decisions to avoid wrongful denies (deny-if-missing disabled during window).
3) Fast rollback: on rollback trigger, runtime flips back to epoch N and replays any in-flight delta reversals. Backfill jobs must support idempotent writes and have a tombstone/marker to skip partial work.
4) Evidence snapshot: at every epoch switch create an evidence bundle (compressed JSON + signature) and emit to SIEM and evidence-storage. This allows reconstructing effective entitlements at any time.

Rollback triggers (automated and manual):
Automated triggers (will initiate automated mitigation and paging):
- SIEM alert: >=5 high-severity authorization-failure spikes in 10m for a single tenant (query in checklist).
- Telemetry: sudden 3x increase in 'denied-by-policy' rate for a route compared to baseline.
- Regression tests: canary evaluation failure (quality gate) after epoch switch.
Manual triggers (SRE/Product/SEC can trigger):
- Customer-sourced escalation (page with reproduction).
- Audit evidence showing privilege widening beyond acceptable delta threshold for tenant.

Automated mitigation steps (on trigger):
1) Immediately mark epoch as quarantined in control-plane to prevent further auto-rollouts.
2) Flip serving epoch pointer back to previous stable epoch (atomic flag in runtime config).
3) Spawn rollback-runbook job: verify that entitlement-store matches epoch snapshot; if mismatch, run corrective reapply.
4) Emit evidence events: rollback.initiated, rollback.completed, rollback.diff-summary to SIEM and evidence storage.
5) Notify on-call and product owners with prefilled incident template.

Preconditions & non-goals:
- Precondition: all entitlement backfill jobs must generate epoch artifacts and signed diffs.
- Non-goal: this doc does not redesign the entitlement data model; it assumes epochs and diffs exist.

SIEM validation checklist (practical queries + expected signals):
Always-on queries (alerting thresholds are tenant-scoped unless noted):
- Deny spike: count(authorization.denied) by tenant over 10m > baseline * 3 AND count > 20 -> alert
- Widening detection: compare(allowed_count(epoch_before), allowed_count(epoch_after)) where percent_increase > 25% -> page SEC
- Backfill dropouts: successful_backfill_jobs(last_30m) < scheduled_jobs(last_30m) -> warn
- Evidence mismatch: number_of_epoch_artifacts_emitted_for_switch != 1 -> warn
- Suspicious ACL churn: count(entitlement.add|remove events) > 500 across tenants in 5m -> investigate (possible bug or mis-scheduled job)

Sample SIEM search snippets (log schema placeholders):
- authorization event: {timestamp, tenant_id, principal_id, resource, action, effect:ALLOW|DENY, reason, epoch_id, trace_id}
- epoch artifact event: {timestamp, epoch_id, origin:backfill|manual, snapshot_hash, signer}
- rollback event: {timestamp, epoch_from, epoch_to, actor, reason, delta_summary}

Suggested SIEM queries (pseudo-SPL):
- deny_spike_query:
  source=authorization | where tenant_id=$TENANT | stats count(eval(effect=="DENY")) by time(10m) | compare_to_baseline("DENY_RATE")
- widening_query:
  idx=entitlements | where epoch_id in (e1,e2) and tenant_id=$TENANT | stats values(allowed_principals) by epoch_id | eval pct_change

Audit payload examples (compact, newline-delimited JSON events to be forwarded to SIEM and evidence store):
- authorization event example:
  {"ts":"2025-02-12T14:05:22Z","tenant":"acme-corp","principal":"user:123","resource":"models/compute","action":"invoke","effect":"DENY","reason":"missing-entitlement","epoch":"epoch-20250212-14-00","trace":"trace-9a8b"}
- epoch artifact example:
  {"ts":"2025-02-12T14:03:00Z","epoch":"epoch-20250212-14-00","origin":"backfill","snapshot_hash":"sha256:abcd...","entries":12453,"signed_by":"backfill-runner-v2"}
- rollback completion example:
  {"ts":"2025-02-12T14:18:01Z","type":"rollback.completed","epoch_from":"epoch-20250212-14-00","epoch_to":"epoch-20250212-13-58","actor":"automation","delta_add":12,"delta_remove":42}

Operational checklist before an epoch switch (pre-launch gating):
- Run canary suite: authorization smoke tests for top 50 routes against canary tenants.
- SIEM preflight: verify that epoch artifact emission hook is green.
- Backfill verification: run dry-run backfill and compare diffs to last known good.
- External hooks: notify Integrations team for any downstream consumers (analytics, billing) that consume entitlements.

Testing & verification matrix:
- Unit: entitlement generator functions (fast feedback) -> devs
- Integration: backfill job -> staging with synthetic tenants -> platform-eng
- Canary: 5% of production tenants for 1hr -> product + sec
- Load: backfill at scale run against replica store -> infra
- SIEM ingest: validate sample payloads in staging SIEM -> observability

Runbook (short):
- If Pager triggers with "deny spike":
  1) Set flag: runtime.deny-if-missing=false for affected tenant(s)
  2) Trigger automated rollback job (UI or CLI: rbac rollback --epoch=previous --tenant=...)
  3) Run evidence check: compare epoch snapshot hash -> if mismatch, run reapply
  4) Post-mortem: open SEC-incident ticket and attach evidence bundle (link in incident template)

Owner matrix and contacts:
- Control plane & rollout logic: Priya Shah (eng-platform)
- Backfill jobs & epochs: Diego Alvarez (eng-served-runtime)
- SIEM ingestion & queries: Jill Park (observability)
- On-call rotation & incident leadership: SRE team (pager)

Open questions / TODOs:
- Tolerance thresholds: should the widening threshold be 25% by default or tenant-specific? (ACTION: product to propose)
- Signed epoch retention: 90 days vs 365 days — compliance wants 365 but storage ops push back. (ACTION: legal + infra)
- Do we record pre-epoch switch traffic samples to help reproduce customer-visible denies? (possible privacy concerns)

Appendix: quick links & commands:
- Evidence download helper: cli: rbac-evidence dump --epoch epoch-20250212-14-00 --tenant acme-corp --out ./evidence.json.gz
- Incident template: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INC/Authorization+Incident+Template
- Jira playbooks: SEC-1187 (backfill validation), ENG-3421 (epoch artifacts)

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally prescriptive: we want teams to have a single agreed rollback pattern and SIEM contract during RBAC v2 rollout. Please flag any incompatible parts with downstream consumers (billing, analytics) before sign-off.
- Draft has some rough areas marked in the TODOs. I expect to iterate after the infra PoC next week.

-- Maya
